news.title: How Gianni Infantino's FIFA leadership imploded over two weeks
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been embroiled in a scandal that has endured for more than two weeks. (Reuters: Dylan Martinez). After weeks of pressure, three of the world's largest continental football confederations have issued a joint open letter attacking the leadership of FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. The presidents and general secretaries of the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) said the saga showed Mr Infantino "places himself above the collection that entrusted him with authority".

news.title: [Official] 'Challenging for Back-to-Back Round of 16' U20 Women's World Cup Final Roster Announced
news.lede: The roster for the South Korean U20 women's national football team competing in the 2026 FIFA U20 Women's World Cup has been announced. The Korea Football Association (KFA) revealed the final 21-player roster to participate in the 2026 FIFA U20 Women's World Cup, which will be held in Poland this September. The head coach is Park Yoon-jeong. The U20 Yeo Ja (CEO) team secured qualification for the World Cup finals by reaching the semifinals of the AFC U20 Women's Asian Cup held in Bangkok, Thailand, last April.

news.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
news.lede: Confederations write open letter damning Fifa president. Concacaf president Montagliani seen as top contender. Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”. In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

news.title: Training Report: Bayern Munich injured stars almost ready; World Cup contingent out a little longer; and MORE!
news.lede: It has been a busy few days for Bayern Munich when it comes to personnel news. News that emerged on Sunday from Säbener Straße indicated that Bayern Munich stars Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala could be back in team training this week (per Bild via @iMiaSanMia): > Among the players currently recovering from injury, Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala are the most advanced in their rehab. Both are expected back in team training at the beginning of the coming week [@BILD] In addition, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia) is reporting that Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano are getting more time off and will not be fully back in action until next week: > Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano have been given more vacation time and won’t return to Munich until the end of the coming week.

news.title: World Cup co-hosts US, Canada oppose Infantino
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has come under intense pressure since first proposing and then shelving a plan to raise private investment for a new commercial subsidiary. (AFP pic) LOS ANGELES: The football federations of the US and Canada - two of the 2026 World Cup host nations - on Monday backed a statement from three confederations criticising Fifa president Gianni Infantino. US Soccer, Canada Soccer, Caribbean Football Union (the CFU) and Central American Football Union (UNCAF) said they "stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens Fifa's governance, transparency and accountability". That puts the US and Canada at odds with the third co-host of this year's World Cup, Mexico, which has given Infantino its backing.
